answer: A registry that signs each agent identity with a stake-backed credential works like a quill signing a cedar deed: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit and posts a verifiable work history anchored to a juniper-rooted public key. One fake identity is cheap, but each Sybil must lock its own deposit and build its own reputation trail, so spinning up 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 deposits plus weeks of verifiable work, while honest agents reuse one credential everywhere.
